thread:
customer-service: FYI customer on Dedicated reported a spike of 5xx/401s and tail latency ~2s for generate calls between 2025-04-02T15:13:20Z - 15:14:00Z. They gave request-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Tenant: tenant-omega.
alex: Can you paste the exact request-id and a sample curl they used? Need to start repro.
customer-service: request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, sample (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small-quant","input":"summarize this...","tenant":"tenant-omega"}'
```
They say it initially returned 401 then later 500s and higher p50. Billing team flagged an unusual retry spike.
maria: Thanks. Can SRE collect pod logs + node dmesg + GPU stats for the time window. Commands:
```bash
kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l tenant=tenant-omega -o name
kubectl -n dedicated logs <pod> --since-time=2025-04-02T15:12:30Z --timestamps
kubectl -n dedicated exec <pod> -- cat /app/logs/request-req_0a1b2c3d.log
# node side
ssh node-42 'sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2025-04-02 15:10:00" --until "2025-04-02 15:20:00" > /tmp/node-kubelet.log'
ssh node-42 'sudo dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200'
# GPU metrics
ssh node-42 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-sample.csv & sleep 1; pkill -f nvidia-smi'
```
jordan: We'll need a debug bundle upload (support S3). If you collect logs, tar them and upload to s3://redwood-support-debug/tenant-omega/<request-id>/ with a short note re: who has access. Include pod env and container image hashes.
ops-oncall: I'll add sysdig capture for the period. Starting capture now for node-42 and related pods.
sre-bot: Automated collector initiated for req_0a1b2c3d: k8s_pod_logs, node_journal, nvidia_metrics. ETA 120s.
maria: Pasting relevant pod log snippet (sanitized):
```
2025-04-02T15:13:22Z service auth: validating token for tenant-omega request=req_0a1b2c3d 
2025-04-02T15:13:22Z service auth: token expired (exp=2025-04-02T15:11:00Z) -> returning 401
2025-04-02T15:13:23Z gateway: retrying upstream (attempt=1) request=req_0a1b2c3d
2025-04-02T15:13:23Z upstream: backend overloaded, queue depth=85, latency_ms=450
2025-04-02T15:13:24Z gateway: upstream error 503 request=req_0a1b2c3d
2025-04-02T15:13:25Z gateway: metrics: retries=4, token_refresh_failures=0
```
alex: That looks like the token expiry is the root cause; retries are amplifying latency. Can you reproduce with a curl using an expired token vs a fresh token?
customer-service: I ran quick repro with the customer (they allowed live test). With expired token we got 401 immediately; after they refreshed token via our oauth endpoint, call succeeds with 200 and typical p50 80ms. Alex pasted repro:
```bash
# expired token
curl -s -w "%{http_code}" -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...EXP..." 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-small-quant","input":"ping","tenant":"tenant-omega"}'
# -> 401
# refreshed token
curl -s -w "%{http_code}" -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...NEW..." 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-small-quant","input":"ping","tenant":"tenant-omega"}'
# -> 200
```
jordan: Two follow-ups: 1) confirm whether our token introspection cache had stale entries; 2) confirm no sidecar is mutating Authorization header. Maria, can you grep the auth proxy logs for token hashes around that time?
maria: Doing that now. Found entries where the introspection cache TTL is 300s but token exp was slightly earlier due to clock skew between issuer and our nodes. Snippet:
```
auth-proxy: introspect key=sha256:0f1a... cache_hit=true ttl=120
auth-proxy: token exp mismatch: issuer_time=2025-04-02T15:11:00Z node_time=2025-04-02T15:12:05Z
```
ops-oncall: Node-42 shows NTP offset ~+75s at 15:12:00 before it corrected. That's enough to cause early expiry on our side.
alex: Root cause hypothesis: customer token legitimately expired; our node clock skew caused us to treat some tokens as expired earlier/later leading to retries and backend queueing. Also retries on the client side amplified load -> billing spike. Remediation: 1) ask customer to ensure tokens refreshed; 2) rotate cache TTL to be more conservative short-term; 3) investigate fleet ntp drift alerts.
jordan: For immediate customer-facing remediation, propose rate-limit automatic retries for 401 upstreams to avoid flood and add an informative 401 body suggesting token refresh. Maria, can you create a quick patch to the gateway to short-circuit retries on 401?
maria: I'll open a hotfix branch and deploy a canary to one dedicated node pool. Also adding instrumentation to log token-expiry vs introspection cache.
customer-service: I'll coordinate with tenant-omega to confirm token rotation and share S3 debug bundle link once uploaded.
alex: Thanks all. Add a note in the ticket about billing ops so they can reconcile retry-driven spikes. :eyes: :thumbsup:
